title: HTTP/2 Connection-Pool Exhaustion — Emergency Operator Runbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This runbook describes operator procedures for diagnosing and mitigating HTTP/2 connection-pool exhaustion in the platform edge and internal service mesh. Connection-pool exhaustion manifests as increased 502/504 errors, spiky tail latency, and large queue depths on GPU serving proxies and API edge routers. The goal is to restore traffic flow and minimize customer impact in under 60 minutes while preserving observable signals required for postmortem.

Scope
-----
- Applies to: edge proxy fleet (ingress-nginx / envoy edge layer), service mesh (envoy sidecars), L7 gateways that use HTTP/2 multiplexing to backends (runtime frontends, model-proxy).
- Not covered: pure TCP-level network partitions, DNS outages, or control-plane API throttles (see separate runbooks).

Impact and Severity Triage
-------------------------
Use these heuristics to set incident severity: 
1) Severity P0: traffic >15% request error rate for production token-generation routes OR multiple large customers reporting end-to-end failures.
2) Severity P1: sustained 5–15% error rate or tail latency (p99.9) spikes >5x baseline for >15 minutes.
3) Severity P2: intermittent 1–5% errors or single-region degradations with graceful fallbacks available.

Observable Symptoms (common signals)
- Surge in 502/504 responses at the edge and sidecar logs showing "upstream reset" or "stream refused"
- Metrics: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_5xx_total, envoy_http_downstream_rq_time_bucket (p99/p99.9), connection_pool.active_connections approaching connection_pool.max (custom metric)
- Queue length/backlog increasing on frontends (platform.request_queue_depth)
- Per-node file descriptors near limit and logs like "too many open files"
- Kernel TCP TIME_WAIT pileup if HTTP/1.1->2 translation misconfigured

Preconditions and Common Root Causes
- Recent config change reducing per-host connection pool size (feature flag, Helm values)
- New client behavior: excessive concurrent streams (improper retry/backoff)
- Upstream backend (model proxy) slowdowns causing long-lived streams and leaking streams
- Envoy upgrade regressions (threading/epoll) or OS-level limits (ulimit, systemd)

Runbook: Immediate actions (0–15 minutes)
--------------------------------------
1) Page the on-call platform operator and set incident channel (#incident-http2-pool).
2) Temporarily enable emergency suppression to stop noisy alerts (do not auto-close). Document suppressed alerts in the channel.
3) Verify customers and regions affected using the tokenized SLI dashboard and recent error logs. Collect the following artifacts:
   - Edge error rate graph (last 60m)
   - Per-node envoy logs (tail last 500 lines)
   - connection_pool.* metrics and process FD counts
4) If error-rate is climbing and backlog > 1000 requests, begin mitigation step A (fast rollback) while investigation runs.

Mitigation step A — Fast rollback (15 minutes)
- When cause is a config or flag change deployed <1hr: rollback that change immediately following the normal rollback checklist.
- Command examples:
  - kubectl rollout status deploy/edge-proxy -n infra
  - git revert <commit> && helm upgrade infra-edge ./charts/edge --reuse-values
- If rollback is not available or the change is not recent, proceed to mitigation step B.

Mitigation step B — Capacity & flow-control hardening (15–45 minutes)
1) Increase connection pool capacity (temporary) on affected envoy clusters. Prioritize regional edge proxies and api-gateway frontends. Example cluster config patch (yaml):
   cluster: 
     name: runtime-frontends
     http2_protocol_options:
       max_concurrent_streams: 512  # raise by 2x as emergency measure
2) Reduce per-request concurrency from upstream with rate-limiting policies: apply a soft limiter to high-traffic routes to reduce new streams. Example: apply a per-route envoy rate-limit (200 rps per tenant)
3) Enable proxy-level stream timeouts to evict stuck streams: set idle_timeout=10s on problematic routes.
4) If nodes show FD exhaustion, increase systemd service limits and restart the process one node at a time:
   - sudo systemctl edit envoy.service  # add LimitNOFILE=65536
   - sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart envoy on nodes in small batches
5) If upgrading max_concurrent_streams is insufficient, temporarily shift traffic to alternate model variants or regions (traffic steering). Use the platform's traffic-split API: POST /admin/traffic-shift

Investigation actions (parallel, 15–60 minutes)
----------------------------------------------
- Query logs for upstream reset causes and stack traces:
  - kubectl logs -l app=runtime-proxy -c envoy --since=1h | grep -i "stream refused\|upstream reset"
- PromQL examples to run in Grafana/Prometheus:
  - sum by(cluster) (rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_5xx_total[5m]))
  - max by(instance) (envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_time_bucket{le="0.999"})
  - sum(node_fd_used) by(instance)
- Check for downstream client behavior: increased concurrent_streams logs from SDKs; correlate with customer API key usage.
- Verify kernel limits and systemd unit config: ulimit -n, cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_max_orphans
- Inspect recent deploys and feature flag changes against the timeline of metric inflection.

Controlled fixes (30–90 minutes)
- If root cause is slow backend: scale up backend pods (replicas) and warm them with synthetic lighter requests to free streams.
  - kubectl scale deployment/model-proxy --replicas=10 -n runtime
- If root cause is client misbehavior, implement a short (1–3 minute) invoker-side concurrency gate and notify customer success for remediation.
- For Envoy/sidecar regressions, pin to last known-good image and rollout with canary of 5% to validate.

Rollback and Safe Restoral
-------------------------
- Any mid-incident config or limit changes must have a documented rollback plan before applying.
- After metrics return to baseline for 15 continuous minutes: gradually revert emergency increases in max_concurrent_streams (step down by 25% every 5 minutes) while observing p99 and error-rate.
- Do not remove alert suppression until the incident commander confirms stability and Slack notes the timeline.

Post-incident tasks and postmortem checklist (owner: incident-commander)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Create a full incident timeline: deploys, flag changes, customer reports, mitigation actions, and metrics snapshots.
- Identify root-cause category (config, backend latency, client, env regression, OS limits).
- Actions to complete within 7 days:
  1) Reproduce in staging with traffic-replay.
  2) Add synthetic benchmarks and a failing test to the pre-deploy gate if the regression was code related.
  3) Implement permanent mitigations (e.g., per-tenant soft-quotas, better backpressure in SDK).
  4) Update SLO / alert thresholds if signal was missing or noisy.
- Owners must assign tickets and due dates in Jira and link them here.

Dashboards and queries to consult (links are placeholders—use local dashboard names)
- Edge: "Edge HTTP/2 Stream Health" — shows max_concurrent_streams usage, p99 latency, and 5xx rate
- Backend: "Model Proxy Stream Lifetimes" — histogram of stream durations and top slow callers
- Node: "Process FD usage and ulimit" — per-node fd_inuse, max_fds
- PromQL quick checks (copy into console):
  - sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_5xx_total[2m])) by(cluster)
  - histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_time_bucket[5m])) by(le, cluster))

Escalation and ownership
------------------------
- First escalation: runtime-oncall (primary) -> eng-platform pager -> runtime-sre lead within 15 minutes.
- If customer-impacting >30 minutes: page customer-success on-call and begin pre-approved tenant notifications.
- Owner for follow-up permanent fixes: runtime-serving team; secondary owner: eng-platform.

Testing and validation of runbook (run quarterly)
------------------------------------------------
- Gameday test: simulate 50% of production traffic replay to staging with artificially reduced max_concurrent_streams and validate operator mitigations within 30 minutes.
- Validation checklist: alerts fire, suppression workflow works, config rollback tested, traffic shift automation validated.

Prevention checklist (permanent controls)
- Enforce pre-deploy gates: SLO regression tests for connection-related metrics.
- Add canary ramping for envoy changes (5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Implement token-aware client backpressure in SDKs (max_streams_per_connection check).
- Work with infra to raise default systemd LimitNOFILE for envoy on all fleets to 65536.

Appendix: example emergency commands and snippets
- Get top nodes by fd usage:
  kubectl top nodes --no-headers | sort -k3 -n | tail -n 10
- Patch envoy cluster via kubectl (one-line):
  kubectl patch configmap envoy-clusters -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"runtime-frontends.yaml":"...updated max_concurrent_streams..."}}'
- Small script to step down emergency value safely (pseudo-shell):
  current=$(curl -s http://config-service/cluster/runtime-frontends | jq .http2.max_concurrent_streams)
  for i in 1 2 3; do new=$((current * (100 - 25*i)/100)); curl -X POST -d "{\"max_concurrent_streams\":$new}" http://config-service/patch; sleep 300; done
